payload.title: Basic timeseries manipulation
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates basic timeseries manipulation using the Pyleoclim library. It focuses on preprocessing a timeseries by standardizing, gaussianizing, and slicing data. The notebook uses sea-surface temperature data from the NINO3 region and provides methods to view summary statistics, standardize, and gaussianize the data. The outputs include visualizations comparing the original, standardized, and gaussianized timeseries.
goals: Learn to specify a slice of a `Series`
Learn to quickly view summary statistics of a `Series`

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduction to basic timeseries manipulation using Pyleoclim, focusing on preprocessing techniques.
section_blurbs.heading: Basic timeseries manipulation

section_blurbs.blurb: Overview of the notebook's goals and relevant packages, including Pyleoclim, Pandas, and Seaborn.
section_blurbs.heading: Preamble

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates how to slice a timeseries using specific date ranges with the `.sel()` method.
section_blurbs.heading: Slicing

section_blurbs.blurb: Shows how to obtain summary statistics of a timeseries using Pyleoclim and Pandas.
section_blurbs.heading: Stats

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains the process of standardizing a timeseries by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.
section_blurbs.heading: Standardizing

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes how to map a timeseries to a standard Gaussian distribution using the `.gaussianize()` method.
section_blurbs.heading: Gaussianize

section_blurbs.blurb: Compares the original, standardized, and gaussianized timeseries using Seaborn for visualization.
section_blurbs.heading: Comparison

inputs: Sea-surface temperature data from the NINO3 region
outputs: Visualizations of original, standardized, and gaussianized timeseries
